title: Area & volume
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Stuck? Open a hint. A wrong answer shows why, and every problem has a worked solution.

problems.prompt: Two angles on a straight line measure $3x$ and $2x + 30$ degrees. What is $x$?

mistakes.why: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$, not $360^\circ$.

problems.prompt: A triangle has base $14$ and height $9$. What is its area?

mistakes.why: A triangle is half of a rectangle: $\frac{1}{2}bh$.

problems.prompt: A box measures $5$ by $4$ by $3$. What is its surface area?

mistakes.why: That is the volume. The surface area adds up the six faces.

hints: There are three pairs of faces: $5 \times 4$, $5 \times 3$ and $4 \times 3$.

problems.prompt: A cube has volume $27$. Each edge is doubled. What is the new volume?

mistakes.why: Volume uses three lengths: doubling each one multiplies the volume by $2^3 = 8$.

hints: Each edge was $3$; now it is $6$.
problems.solution: The edge goes from $3$ to $6$, so the volume is $6^3 = 216$ (that is $27 \times 8$).

title: Area & volume: PSAT questions
instructions: Four PSAT-style questions with choices (A) to (D), easiest first. You can leave a question blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each question.

problems.prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure $48^\circ$ and $67^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?

why.C: That is the sum of the two angles. Subtract it from $180$.
why.D: A triangle’s angles add up to $180^\circ$, not $360^\circ$.

problems.prompt: A circle has area $49\pi$. What is its circumference?

why.A: The radius is $7$; the circumference is $2\pi r$.

problems.solution: $\pi r^2 = 49\pi$, so $r = 7$ and the circumference is $2\pi \times 7 = 14\pi$, choice (B).

problems.prompt: A cone has radius $3$ and height $8$. What is its volume?

why.C: That is the cylinder. A cone is $\frac{1}{3}$ of it.

problems.prompt: A rectangular pool is $10$ m long, $4$ m wide and $2$ m deep. How many cubic metres of water fill it?

why.A: Multiply the three lengths; don’t add them.
why.B: That is the area of the bottom. Multiply by the depth.

title: Right triangles & trigonometry
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Stuck? Open a hint. A wrong answer shows why, and every problem has a worked solution.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs $9$ and $12$. How long is the hypotenuse?

mistakes.why: Square, add, then take the square root: $\sqrt{81 + 144}$.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse $26$ and one leg $10$. How long is the other leg?
In right triangle $PQR$ the right angle is at $R$, $PR = 8$ and $PQ = 17$. What is $\sin Q$?

mistakes.why: That is $\cos Q$. Sine uses the side OPPOSITE $Q$, which is $PR$.

problems.prompt: In a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle the shortest side is $7$. How long is the hypotenuse?
problems.solution: The hypotenuse is twice the shortest side: $14$.

title: Right triangles & trigonometry: PSAT questions
instructions: Four PSAT-style questions with choices (A) to (D), easiest first. You can leave a question blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each question.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs $8$ and $15$. How long is the hypotenuse?

why.C: Add the squares; don’t subtract them.
why.D: That is $c^2$. Take the square root.

problems.prompt: In right triangle $XYZ$ with the right angle at $Z$, $\tan X = \frac{3}{4}$. What is $\sin X$?
problems.solution: Opposite $3$ and adjacent $4$ give hypotenuse $5$, so $\sin X = \frac{3}{5}$, choice (A).

problems.prompt: If $\sin x^\circ = 0.6$, what is $\cos(90 - x)^\circ$?

why.C: That would be $\cos x^\circ$. Here the angle is $90 - x$.
why.A: Sine and cosine don’t add up to $1$.

problems.solution: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement, so $\cos(90 - x)^\circ = 0.6$, choice (B).

problems.prompt: A square has a diagonal of length $10$. What is its side length?

why.A: The diagonal is $\sqrt{2}$ times the side, not twice.

problems.solution: A diagonal splits the square into two $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangles, so $s\sqrt{2} = 10$ and $s = \frac{10}{\sqrt{2}} = 5\sqrt{2}$, choice (B).

title: Circles
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Stuck? Open a hint. A wrong answer shows why, and every problem has a worked solution.

problems.prompt: A circle has circumference $18\pi$. What is its radius?

mistakes.why: That is the diameter. The circumference is $2\pi r$: divide by $2\pi$.

problems.prompt: A circle has radius $10$. An arc has a central angle of $72^\circ$, and its length is $k\pi$. What is $k$?

mistakes.why: That is the whole circumference over $\pi$. Take $\frac{72}{360}$ of it.

problems.prompt: A sector of a circle with radius $6$ has a central angle of $120^\circ$, and its area is $k\pi$. What is $k$?

mistakes.why: Area uses $\pi r^2 = 36\pi$, not the circumference.

problems.prompt: The circle $(x + 4)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 49$ has centre $(h, k)$. What is $h + k$?

title: Circles: PSAT questions
instructions: Four PSAT-style questions with choices (A) to (D), easiest first. You can leave a question blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each question.

problems.prompt: What is the radius of the circle $(x - 2)^2 + (y + 5)^2 = 36$?

why.C: That is $r^2$. Take the square root.
why.B: Take the square root of $36$, don’t halve it.

problems.prompt: How many radians is $135^\circ$?
A circle has diameter $20$. What is the area of a sector with a central angle of $90^\circ$?

why.D: That is the whole circle. A $90^\circ$ sector is a quarter of it.
why.A: That is a quarter of the circumference, not of the area.

problems.solution: The radius is $10$, so the circle’s area is $100\pi$; a quarter is $25\pi$, choice (B).

problems.prompt: Which is an equation of the circle with centre $(-1, 3)$ and radius $4$?

why.A: The signs inside the brackets are the opposite of the centre’s.
